reviewQuestions: Are conformity pathways and prerequisites correctly modeled?
Are CE marking and registration gates non-automatic?
scope: conformity-assessment pathways for applicable high-risk systems
EU declaration of conformity, CE marking and registration sequence
evidence and approval gates preventing false completion
officialSources: applicable Annex VI or VII pathways and product-sector legislation

preReviewFindings.finding: The platform must never issue or imply formal conformity, CE marking or registration authority.
preReviewFindings.requiredDecision: Approve fail-closed gates and all non-certification wording.

preReviewFindings.finding: Applicable pathway depends on system category, harmonised standards, common specifications and sector law.
preReviewFindings.requiredDecision: Confirm decision inputs and mandatory external-assessor escalation.

preReviewFindings.finding: Commercial materials and contracts must describe conformity support consistently.
preReviewFindings.requiredDecision: Align approved claims and contractual scope after founder facts are confirmed.

acceptanceCriteria: No automatic conformity or CE outcome exists.
Pathway prerequisites and notified-body dependencies are accurate.
Registration follows only after valid external prerequisites.
Marketing and contract wording matches the technical boundary.
humanInputsRequired: notified-body or sector-specialist input when applicable
limitations: Risck Comply is not a notified body or market-surveillance authority.
The product cannot issue a declaration of conformity or CE marking.
External standards and sector-law evidence remain outside repository proof.
